datasets.label: Derived corona · Oct 2015
datasets.title: ι Horologii’s corona, derived from its magnetic field of Oct 2015
datasets.description: No telescope has imaged this corona, and this is not a published result: it is derived here from the star's magnetic map by a standard method. The map of the star's surface magnetic field from Oct 2015 (Alvarado-Gómez et al. · HARPSpol) is continued outward as a field with no electric currents, out to 2.5 stellar radii, where the wind is taken to pull it straight. Gas at rest fills a sheet about the line where that field reverses, as the Sun's bright streamers do; the wind fills the rest. How much gas there is follows from three numbers. The star's X-ray output is measured (Freund et al. (2022), A&A 664, A105). Its coronal temperature, 4.4 million kelvin, is not measured: it is the temperature stars of this X-ray output have (Johnstone & Güdel (2015), A&A 578, A129). Its mass loss, 25 times the Sun's, is not measured either: it is what the X-ray output suggests (Wood et al. (2021), ApJ 915, 37). Stars with a measured wind lie within a factor of 5 of that relation, and one is 38 times below it. It is shown the way coronagraph pictures are: at each distance from the star brightness is proportional to the density there, and only the steep fall-off with distance is compressed. The method was tested on the one star with a published simulation of its corona, ε Eridani, where its density is within a factor of two of the simulation's on average, and on the Sun, whose corona is measured dense along the same line. The rotation axis is 60° from the line of sight, as the map was fitted, and the corona is drawn in the same frame as the star's own maps; where the axis points on the sky and the star's rotation phase today are conventions.
